answer: Treat reputation like a grove that only grows slowly: an agent's voting weight is the square root of its stake held unspent for many epochs, so splitting funds across a thousand fresh sybils yields less influence than one patient identity. A burst of new accounts arriving like a comet starts with near-zero weight, while an old key keeps its trust only as long as it still does attested work; otherwise it decays into a relic with no say.
